text:
maya: FYI emb+rerank lanes in us-west are flapping — throttle spikes ~3x, and customers are getting bounced between small and large pools repeatedly. perf dash: https://dash.redwood/internal/emb-rerank :eyes:
jorge: Can you share p95 token latency and lane assignment churn numbers?
maya: p95 token latency jumped 210ms -> 380ms during spike. lane churn shows moves every ~30s for ~20 customers. throttles surged from 120 -> 1320 in the hour.
katie: Is this tied to that credit-admission tweak we rolled last week? softlimit changes? :thinking:
maya: Yes, the release is release-emb-credit-2026-03-15. My hypothesis: credit window was set too tight for bursty fanout workloads, causing fast refill + preemption oscillation.
ellie: We saw the same pattern in eu-west months ago. Credit-only admission without smoothing causes bang-bang behavior. Recommend leaky-bucket smoothing + per-tenant min-reserve.
sam: We can try a short-term smoothing + token reservation. Sketch config we could push to the admission controller:
```
admission:
  type: credit-leaky
  burst_tokens: 100
  refill_rate: 20/s
  reserve_per_tenant: 10
  preemption_cooldown: 30s
```
jorge: Also seeing queue depth oscillation when preemption moves jobs between lanes. Move triggers reclaim, which creates new backlog and more preemption. vicious loop.
maya: Immediate mitigations I propose: disable aggressive preemption for large-rerank lane, bump burst_tokens to 200 for customers with SLA tags, and enable fallback to quantized rerank model for non-SLA tenants to reduce pressure.
katie: I'll patch the autoscaler logic to avoid scale-downs within a 3m window during high churn and add a cooldown for lane preemption.
ops-bot: alert: emb-rerank-throttle count=1320 affected_customers=27 link=https://alerts.redwood/12345
maya: Assigning owners: @sam for admission config change, @katie for autoscaler patch, @ellie to validate fallback model quality. We'll reconvene in 30m to decide incident escalation.
ellie: On it — running quick A/B of quantized fallback against a sample of recent queries to check regression rates.
sam: Config PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/452 :thumbsup:
katie: Temporary suppress rule added to avoid noisy alerts. If throttles don't drop in 20m we'll open an incident.
